1. # Evaluations
2. 
3. Evaluations measure how well an LLM uses your MCP server's tools to answer questions.
4. 
5. ## Evaluation Format
6. 
7. Use XML with `qa_pair` elements:
8. 
9. ```xml
10. <evaluations>
11.   <qa_pair>
12.     <question>What are the top 3 products in the Electronics category by price?</question>
13.     <answer>The top 3 products are: 1. Ultra HD TV ($1,299), 2. Gaming Laptop ($1,199), 3. Wireless Headphones ($349).</answer>
14.   </qa_pair>
15.   <qa_pair>
16.     <question>How many products cost less than $50 and are currently in stock?</question>
17.     <answer>There are 12 products under $50 that are currently in stock.</answer>
18.   </qa_pair>
19. </evaluations>
20. ```
21. 
22. ## Writing Good Evaluation Questions
23. 
24. **Questions must be read-only, non-destructive, and deterministic.** The LLM should be able to verify its answer against a known correct result without modifying any data.
25. 
26. ### Principles
27. 
28. | Principle | Good Example | Bad Example |
29. |-----------|-------------|-------------|
30. | Read-only | "List all products in category X" | "Add a new product to category X" |
31. | Deterministic | "What is the price of product #123?" | "What's a good product to buy?" |
32. | Multi-tool | "Which category has the highest average price?" (requires listing categories + querying each) | "What is product #1?" (single lookup) |
33. | Verifiable | "How many products have rating > 4.5?" | "Describe the best products" |
34. 
35. ### Design Tips
36. 
37. - **Require reasoning across multiple tool calls** — e.g., "Compare the average price of Electronics vs. Books" needs two category queries plus computation.
38. - **Include edge cases** — empty results, boundary values, special characters in search terms.
39. - **Vary complexity** — mix simple single-tool questions with multi-step reasoning chains.
40. - **Answers must be precise** — include exact values, counts, or names that can be verified programmatically.
41. 
42. ### Example: Product Catalog Evaluations
43. 
44. ```xml
45. <evaluations>
46.   <qa_pair>
47.     <question>What is the most expensive product across all categories?</question>
48.     <answer>The most expensive product is the Ultra HD TV in Electronics at $1,299.99.</answer>
49.   </qa_pair>
50.   <qa_pair>
51.     <question>Which categories contain products that are out of stock? List the category names and the count of out-of-stock items in each.</question>
52.     <answer>Electronics has 3 out-of-stock items, Books has 1 out-of-stock item.</answer>
53.   </qa_pair>
54.   <qa_pair>
55.     <question>Find all products with "wireless" in the name and sort them by price ascending.</question>
56.     <answer>1. Wireless Mouse ($24.99), 2. Wireless Keyboard ($49.99), 3. Wireless Headphones ($349.00).</answer>
57.   </qa_pair>
58. </evaluations>
59. ```
60.

 Evaluations measure how well an LLM uses your MCP server's tools to answer questions.

 ```xml
     <answer>There are 12 products under $50 that are currently in stock.</answer>
   </qa_pair>
 </evaluations>
 ```
 
 ## Writing Good Evaluation Questions
 
 **Questions must be read-only, non-destructive, and deterministic.** The LLM should be able to verify its answer against a known correct result without modifying any data.
 
 ### Principles
 
 | Principle | Good Example | Bad Example |
 |-----------|-------------|-------------|

 | Verifiable | "How many products have rating > 4.5?" | "Describe the best products" |

1. # Evaluators catalog
2. 
3. Full catalog of evaluators wired by `setup-maf-evals`, grouped by tier.
4. The skill defaults to Tier 1 (NLP) always on, Tier 2 (Quality) on but
5. gated by `EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE`, Tier 3 (Safety) off unless opted in.
6. 
7. Source: [learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/ai/evaluation/libraries](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/ai/evaluation/libraries)
8. 
9. ## Tier 1 — NLP (deterministic, no LLM)
10. 
11. Package: `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation.NLP` (preview 10.7.0).
12. 
13. | Evaluator | Metric | Context type needed | Notes |
14. |-----------|--------|---------------------|-------|
15. | `BLEUEvaluator` | `BLEU` | `BLEUEvaluatorContext(IEnumerable<string> references)` | n-gram overlap with one or more reference strings |
16. | `GLEUEvaluator` | `GLEU` | `GLEUEvaluatorContext(IEnumerable<string> references)` | sentence-level BLEU variant |
17. | `F1Evaluator` | `F1` | `F1EvaluatorContext(string groundTruth)` | unigram-level F1 |
18. 
19. Plus a built-in custom evaluator the skill always scaffolds:
20. 
21. | Evaluator | Metric | Why |
22. |-----------|--------|-----|
23. | `WordCountEvaluator` (custom) | `Words` | Sanity check: response is non-empty and reasonable length. Same pattern as the Learn doc tutorial. |
24. 
25. ### `WordCountEvaluator` reference implementation
26. 
27. Scaffold this file verbatim (the Learn-doc canonical pattern) into
28. `Reporting/WordCountEvaluator.cs`. It runs in stub tier with no API key.
29. 
30. ```csharp
31. public sealed class WordCountEvaluator : IEvaluator
32. {
33.     public const string MetricName = "Words";
34.     public IReadOnlyCollection<string> EvaluationMetricNames { get; } = [MetricName];
35. 
36.     public ValueTask<EvaluationResult> EvaluateAsync(
37.         IEnumerable<ChatMessage> messages,
38.         ChatResponse modelResponse,
39.         ChatConfiguration? chatConfiguration = null,
40.         IEnumerable<EvaluationContext>? additionalContext = null,
41.         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
42.     {
43.         var text = modelResponse?.Text ?? string.Empty;
44.         var count = text.Split(
45.             new[] { ' ', '\t', '\r', '\n' },
46.             StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries).Length;
47. 
48.         var metric = new NumericMetric(MetricName, value: count)
49.         {
50.             Interpretation = count switch
51.             {
52.                 < 5   => new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(EvaluationRating.Poor,    reason: "Response too short"),
53.                 > 500 => new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(EvaluationRating.Average, reason: "Response very long"),
54.                 _     => new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(EvaluationRating.Good),
55.             }
56.         };
57.         return new ValueTask<EvaluationResult>(new EvaluationResult(metric));
58.     }
59. }
60. ```
61. 
62. ## Tier 2 — Quality (LLM-as-judge)
63. 
64. Package: `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation.Quality` (GA 10.7.0).
65. 
66. Requires `EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE=1` and a real `IChatClient`. The skill
67. wires the following by default:
68. 
69. | Evaluator | Metric | Context type | Notes |
70. |-----------|--------|--------------|-------|
71. | `RelevanceEvaluator` | `Relevance` | none | how relevant is the response to the query |
72. | `CoherenceEvaluator` | `Coherence` | none | logical, orderly presentation |
73. | `FluencyEvaluator` | `Fluency` | none | grammar, readability |
74. | `CompletenessEvaluator` | `Completeness` | `CompletenessEvaluatorContext(string groundTruth)` | comprehensive and accurate |
75. | `EquivalenceEvaluator` | `Equivalence` | `EquivalenceEvaluatorContext(string groundTruth)` | similarity vs ground truth wrt query |
76. | `GroundednessEvaluator` | `Groundedness` | `GroundednessEvaluatorContext(string context)` | alignment with given context |
77. 
78. Agent-focused (added when `*.AppHost.csproj` is detected, indicating
79. this is an agentic app and not just a chat completion app):
80. 
81. | Evaluator | Metric | Context type | Notes |
82. |-----------|--------|--------------|-------|
83. | `IntentResolutionEvaluator` | `Intent Resolution` | none | identifies + resolves user intent |
84. | `TaskAdherenceEvaluator` | `Task Adherence` | none | sticks to assigned task |
85. | `ToolCallAccuracyEvaluator` | `Tool Call Accuracy` | `ToolCallAccuracyEvaluatorContext(...)` | uses tools correctly |
86. 
87. **Not wired by default:** `RelevanceTruthAndCompletenessEvaluator`
88. (marked experimental in upstream docs), `RetrievalEvaluator` (specific
89. to RAG pipelines — separate skill territory).
90. 
91. ## Tier 3 — Safety (Foundry Evaluation service)
92. 
93. Package: `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation.Safety` (preview 10.7.0).
94. 
95. Off by default. Enabled when user opts in during step 2 of the
96. workflow. Requires `EVAL_USE_FOUNDRY_SAFETY=1` and an Azure AI Foundry
97. endpoint (the skill prompts for `AZURE_AI_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT` + Entra credentials).
98. 
99. **Always wire the bundle, not the 4 separate evaluators:**
100. 
101. | Evaluator | Metrics produced | Notes |
102. |-----------|------------------|-------|
103. | `ContentHarmEvaluator` | `Hate And Unfairness`, `Self Harm`, `Violence`, `Sexual` | **Single-shot — one Foundry call returns all 4 metrics.** Always prefer this over the 4 separate evaluators below. |
104. 
105. Additional safety evaluators (each wired as separate `[TestMethod]`):
106. 
107. | Evaluator | Metric | Notes |
108. |-----------|--------|-------|
109. | `ProtectedMaterialEvaluator` | `Protected Material` | copyrighted material in output |
110. | `IndirectAttackEvaluator` | `Indirect Attack` | prompt-injection-style indirect attacks |
111. | `CodeVulnerabilityEvaluator` | `Code Vulnerability` | vulnerable code in output |
112. | `UngroundedAttributesEvaluator` | `Ungrounded Attributes` | inferred human attributes |
113. | `GroundednessProEvaluator` | `Groundedness Pro` | fine-tuned Foundry-hosted groundedness check |
114. 
115. The 4 separate evaluators (`HateAndUnfairnessEvaluator`,
116. `SelfHarmEvaluator`, `ViolenceEvaluator`, `SexualEvaluator`) are
117. **not** scaffolded — they're a strict subset of `ContentHarmEvaluator`
118. and cost 4× more Foundry calls for the same metrics.
119. 
120. ## Threshold mapping
121. 
122. `quality.thresholds.json` maps **real MEAI metric names** to minimum
123. `EvaluationRating` enum values:
124. 
125. ```json
126. {
127.   "schema_version": 2,
128.   "hard_fail": false,
129.   "thresholds": {
130.     "Relevance":   { "min_rating": "Good" },
131.     "Coherence":   { "min_rating": "Good" },
132.     "Fluency":     { "min_rating": "Average" },
133.     "Groundedness":{ "min_rating": "Good" },
134.     "BLEU":        { "min_value": 0.20 },
135.     "F1":          { "min_value": 0.30 },
136.     "Words":       { "min_value": 5, "max_value": 500 }
137.   }
138. }
139. ```
140. 
141. `hard_fail: true` makes any below-threshold metric fail the test.
142. Default `false` makes the test pass-through informational — failures
143. show in the report only.
144. 
145. ## Custom rubric-driven evaluator
146. 
147. The built-in Quality evaluators (Relevance, Coherence, Fluency,
148. Completeness, Equivalence) judge against generic rubrics baked into
149. the evaluator's judge prompt. They cannot read `Quality/rubric.md`.
150. That makes them ill-fitting for agents with deliberate stylistic
151. constraints (ELI5 / summarizer / strict-format / persona-bound
152. agents) — see `common-pitfalls.md#tuning-quality-for-stylistic-agents`.
153. 
154. For those agents, scaffold a `RubricEvaluator` that reads
155. `Quality/rubric.md` and asks the judge to score against *your*
156. criteria. The pattern is shape-identical to `WordCountEvaluator` —
157. it just delegates to the judge chat client.
158. 
159. ```csharp
160. // Reporting/RubricEvaluator.cs
161. // Custom rubric-driven evaluator. Reads Quality/rubric.md and asks
162. // the judge to score the response against per-app criteria. Emits a
163. // single "RubricFit" metric (numeric 1-5) plus a free-text rationale.
164. public sealed class RubricEvaluator : IEvaluator
165. {
166.     public const string MetricName = "RubricFit";
167.     public IReadOnlyCollection<string> EvaluationMetricNames { get; } = [MetricName];
168. 
169.     private readonly string _rubric;
170. 
171.     public RubricEvaluator(string rubricMarkdown) => _rubric = rubricMarkdown;
172. 
173.     public static RubricEvaluator FromFile(string path) =>
174.         new(File.ReadAllText(path));
175. 
176.     public async ValueTask<EvaluationResult> EvaluateAsync(
177.         IEnumerable<ChatMessage> messages,
178.         ChatResponse modelResponse,
179.         ChatConfiguration? chatConfiguration = null,
180.         IEnumerable<EvaluationContext>? additionalContext = null,
181.         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
182.     {
183.         if (chatConfiguration?.ChatClient is null)
184.         {
185.             // Judge tier not active — return a stubbed Inconclusive metric.
186.             return new EvaluationResult(new NumericMetric(MetricName)
187.             {
188.                 Interpretation = new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(
189.                     EvaluationRating.Inconclusive, reason: "Judge not wired.")
190.             });
191.         }
192. 
193.         var userQuery = string.Join("\n", messages.Select(m => m.Text));
194.         var responseText = modelResponse.Text ?? string.Empty;
195. 
196.         // NOTE: $$"""...""" (double-$) raw string. Inside, single { } is literal
197.         // (matters for the JSON braces below), and {{var}} is interpolation.
198.         // Plain $"""...""" would reject `{{ ... }}` as literal with CS9006.
199.         var prompt = $$"""
200.             You are scoring an assistant response against the rubric below.
201. 
202.             ## Rubric
203.             {{_rubric}}
204. 
205.             ## User query
206.             {{userQuery}}
207. 
208.             ## Assistant response
209.             {{responseText}}
210. 
211.             Respond with strict JSON: { "score": <1-5 int>, "rationale": "<1-2 sentences>" }.
212.             5 = perfectly satisfies every rubric clause. 1 = ignores the rubric.
213.             """;
214. 
215.         var judge = await chatConfiguration.ChatClient.GetResponseAsync(
216.             prompt, cancellationToken: cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
217. 
218.         // Tolerant parse: fall back to Inconclusive on bad JSON.
219.         var (score, rationale) = TryParse(judge.Text ?? "");
220. 
221.         var metric = new NumericMetric(MetricName, value: score)
222.         {
223.             Interpretation = new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(
224.                 rating: score switch { >= 4 => EvaluationRating.Good,
225.                                        3    => EvaluationRating.Average,
226.                                        _    => EvaluationRating.Poor },
227.                 reason: rationale)
228.         };
229.         return new EvaluationResult(metric);
230.     }
231. 
232.     private static (int score, string rationale) TryParse(string raw)
233.     {
234.         try
235.         {
236.             using var doc = JsonDocument.Parse(raw.Trim().Trim('`', ' ', '\n', '\r'));
237.             return (doc.RootElement.GetProperty("score").GetInt32(),
238.                     doc.RootElement.GetProperty("rationale").GetString() ?? "");
239.         }
240.         catch { return (3, "Judge response was unparseable; defaulted to Average."); }
241.     }
242. }
243. ```
244. 
245. Wire it from `Reporting/ReportingConfig.cs`'s judge-tier evaluator
246. list **alongside** Relevance/Coherence/Fluency (drop Completeness +
247. Equivalence per the pitfall guidance):
248. 
249. ```csharp
250. // In ReportingConfig.ForQuality(), when EvalEnv.UseRealJudge:
251. evaluators.Add(new RelevanceEvaluator());
252. evaluators.Add(new CoherenceEvaluator());
253. evaluators.Add(new FluencyEvaluator());
254. evaluators.Add(RubricEvaluator.FromFile(
255.     Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "Quality", "rubric.md")));
256. // CompletenessEvaluator + EquivalenceEvaluator deliberately dropped
257. // for this app — see common-pitfalls.md tuning section.
258. ```
259. 
260. Ensure `Quality/rubric.md` is copied to output by adding to the csproj:
261. 
262. ```xml
263. <ItemGroup>
264.   <None Update="Quality/rubric.md" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
265. </ItemGroup>
266. ```
267. 
268. This `RubricFit` metric will appear in `report.html` alongside the
269. built-ins, and the rationale shows in the per-scenario detail drawer.
270. Update `Reporting/MetricsGlossary.cs`'s `QualityEntries` constant to
271. add a one-line `RubricFit` definition pointing at `Quality/rubric.md`.
272.

 # skill-validator
 
 You've built a bunch of skills. But are they actually helping or just adding noise?
 
 **skill-validator** finds out. It runs your agent with and without each skill, measures what changed, and tells you whether the skill is worth keeping.
 
 Plugging into your CI, it ensures every new skill adds real value, and existing skills that stop helping when a new model comes out can be removed.
 
 ## How it works
 
 1. Discovers skills (directories with `SKILL.md`)
 2. Reads evaluation scenarios from each skill's `tests/eval.yaml`

 4. Collects metrics: token usage, tool calls, time, errors, task completion
 5. Uses **pairwise comparative judging** — the LLM judge sees both outputs side-by-side and decides which is better (with position-swap bias mitigation)
 6. Computes **confidence intervals** via bootstrapping across multiple runs
 7. Compares results and produces a verdict with statistical significance

 ### Download from pipeline artifacts
 
 A nightly scheduled job publishes AOT-compiled .tar.gz archives and NuGet packages as assets on the [`skill-validator-nightly` GitHub Release](https://github.com/dotnet/skills/releases/tag/skill-validator-nightly).

 ```bash
 skill-validator evaluate --baseline-from baseline.json --tests-dir ./tests/my-plugin ./plugins/my-plugin/skills/skill-b
 ```

1. # IChatClient detection
2. 
3. The skill auto-detects how the target app registers its `IChatClient`
4. and emits `Wire/AgentChatClientFactory.cs` so `EVAL_USE_REAL_AGENT=1`
5. works without further code. Detection result is surfaced in step 2
6. (scope confirmation) and can be overridden by the user.
7. 
8. ## Patterns to scan for
9. 
10. Scan **`*.AppHost.csproj` directory** and **all `*.Agent*.csproj`
11. directories**. Match (case-insensitive, multi-line):
12. 
13. | Pattern (regex-ish) | Inferred client | Example file:line |
14. |---------------------|-----------------|--------------------|
15. | `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient\s*\(` or `AddAzureOpenAIClient\s*\(` | Azure OpenAI | `AppHost.cs`, `Program.cs` |
16. | `AddOpenAIChatClient\s*\(` | OpenAI direct | `Program.cs` |
17. | `AddOllamaChatClient\s*\(` | Ollama | `Program.cs` |
18. | `AddAIInference\s*\(` (Foundry deployment alias) | Azure AI Foundry | `AppHost.cs` |
19. | `AddAzureChatCompletionsClient\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\.AddChatClient\s*\(` | Aspire `Aspire.Azure.AI.Inference` (Foundry-routed, **legacy — see deprecation note below**) | `Program.cs` |
20. | `AddOpenAIClient\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\.AddChatClient\s*\(` | Aspire OpenAI/v1 (Foundry-routed via the OpenAI SDK) | `Program.cs` |
21. | `services\.AddSingleton<IChatClient>` (any explicit registration) | custom | varies |
22. | `\.AsIChatClient\(\)` (after an SDK client) | manual wrap | varies |
23. 
24. > The `AddAzureChatCompletionsClient(...).AddChatClient(...)` chain is the
25. > Aspire 13.2 way of wiring an `IChatClient` against a Foundry chat
26. > deployment via the `Azure.AI.Inference` beta SDK. The argument is the
27. > **connection-string name**, which Aspire's AppHost populates
28. > automatically (`AddDeployment("chat", ...)` -> connection string `chat`).
29. > The factory mirrors both calls verbatim.
30. >
31. > ⚠️ **Deprecation note (as of 2026):** the `Azure.AI.Inference` beta SDK
32. > is being retired on **August 26, 2026** in favor of the GA OpenAI/v1
33. > API + stable OpenAI SDK. New apps should prefer the
34. > `AddOpenAIClient(...).AddChatClient(...)` pattern against an OpenAI/v1
35. > endpoint, which avoids several quirks (notably the reasoning-model
36. > `max_tokens` rejection documented in
37. > `references/common-pitfalls.md`). The skill still detects and supports
38. > the legacy pattern unchanged. See the
39. > [Foundry migration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/model-inference-to-openai-migration).
40. 
41. Capture the deployment alias / model id literal if present (e.g.,
42. `builder.AddAIInference("chat", "gpt-4o-mini")` → alias `chat`).
43. 
44. ## What to emit
45. 
46. ### Case A — exactly one registration found
47. 
48. Emit a factory that resolves from the host:
49. 
50. ```csharp
51. // Wire/AgentChatClientFactory.cs
52. namespace {{AppName}}.Evals.Tests;
53. 
54. internal static class AgentChatClientFactory
55. {
56.     /// <summary>
57.     /// Resolves the same IChatClient the app uses, by building a minimal
58.     /// host that mirrors the app's DI registration.
59.     /// Detected: {{DetectionSummary}} at {{File}}:{{Line}}
60.     /// </summary>
61.     public static IChatClient Create()
62.     {
63.         var builder = Host.CreateApplicationBuilder();
64. 
65.         // In test hosts (`dotnet test`), the entry assembly is testhost.exe so
66.         // user-secrets are NOT auto-loaded by CreateApplicationBuilder.
67.         // Add them explicitly from THIS assembly's UserSecretsId.
68.         builder.Configuration.AddUserSecrets(typeof(AgentChatClientFactory).Assembly, optional: true);
69. 
70.         // {{InsertDetectedRegistrationCallVerbatim}}
71.         var host = builder.Build();
72.         try
73.         {
74.             return host.Services.GetRequiredService<IChatClient>();
75.         }
76.         catch (InvalidOperationException ex)
77.         {
78.             throw new InvalidOperationException(
79.                 "EVAL_USE_REAL_AGENT=1 but IChatClient could not be resolved. " +
80.                 "The detected registration ({{DetectionSummary}}) reads connection " +
81.                 "string \"{{ConnStrName}}\" from configuration. Aspire's AppHost " +
82.                 "populates this at runtime, but `dotnet test` runs standalone. " +
83.                 "Wire one of:\n" +
84.                 "  # Key-based auth (only if the resource has it enabled):\n" +
85.                 "  dotnet user-secrets set \"ConnectionStrings:{{ConnStrName}}\" " +
86.                 "\"Endpoint=https://<host>.services.ai.azure.com/models;Key=<key>;DeploymentId={{ConnStrName}}\" --project {{AppName}}.Evals.Tests\n" +
87.                 "  # Entra-ID auth (DefaultAzureCredential — works when key auth is disabled):\n" +
88.                 "  dotnet user-secrets set \"ConnectionStrings:{{ConnStrName}}\" " +
89.                 "\"Endpoint=https://<host>.services.ai.azure.com/models;DeploymentId={{ConnStrName}}\" --project {{AppName}}.Evals.Tests\n" +
90.                 "Note: the hostname strips dashes from the resource name " +
91.                 "(resource `foundry-abc` -> host `foundryabc.services.ai.azure.com`).\n" +
92.                 "Get the exact endpoint from `azd env get-values` or " +
93.                 "`az cognitiveservices account show -n <name> -g <rg> --query properties.endpoints`.",
94.                 ex);
95.         }
96.     }
97. }
98. ```
99. 
100. Where `{{InsertDetectedRegistrationCallVerbatim}}` is the literal call
101. copied from the detection source (with any required `using`s in scope
102. via `GlobalUsings.cs`), and `{{ConnStrName}}` is the connection-string
103. literal extracted from the call (e.g., the `"chat"` argument).
104. 
105. ### Case B — multiple registrations found
106. 
107. Emit the same factory but with a comment listing all candidates, and
108. have the chat output ask the user to pick one before write. Do **not**
109. write the file until confirmation.
110. 
111. ### Case C — no registration found
112. 
113. Emit a stub factory the user fills in:
114. 
115. ```csharp
116. // Wire/AgentChatClientFactory.cs
117. namespace {{AppName}}.Evals.Tests;
118. 
119. internal static class AgentChatClientFactory
120. {
121.     /// <summary>
122.     /// Auto-detection failed: no IChatClient registration found in
123.     /// AppHost or agent projects. Wire your client manually.
124.     /// </summary>
125.     public static IChatClient Create() =>
126.         throw new NotImplementedException(
127.             "Wire your IChatClient here. See https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/ai/microsoft-extensions-ai");
128. }
129. ```
130. 
131. ## Runtime selection
132. 
133. `ReportingConfig` picks agent client based on tier:
134. 
135. ```csharp
136. internal static IChatClient ResolveAgentClient() =>
137.     EvalEnv.UseRealAgent ? AgentChatClientFactory.Create() : new StubChatClient();
138. ```
139. 
140. And by default the judge client is the **same** instance as the agent
141. client. This saves a duplicate Azure credential setup AND lets the
142. MEAI response cache serve both the agent call and the judge call from
143. one cache (because `QualityTests` uses `run.ChatConfiguration!.ChatClient`
144. for the agent call — that's the cached wrapper around the shared
145. instance). The user can override by setting `EVAL_JUDGE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME`
146. to a different deployment alias when (e.g.) the production model is a
147. reasoning model that can't be used as a judge. Trade-off: with the
148. override active, `run.ChatConfiguration!.ChatClient` becomes the
149. **judge** client, so the agent call would silently use the judge
150. model. To avoid that, `QualityTests` falls back to
151. `Wire.ResolveAgentClient()` (uncached) for agent calls whenever the
152. override is set; cache hits then apply only to judge calls.
153. 
154. ## Connection-string setup for standalone test runs
155. 
156. When the target app uses Aspire orchestration, the AppHost populates
157. `ConnectionStrings:<alias>` automatically. **`dotnet test` runs outside
158. the AppHost and does not get this for free.** Surface this in the chat
159. output any time the detected pattern reads from a connection string
160. (`AddAzureChatCompletionsClient`, `AddAIInference`, `AddOllamaChatClient`,
161. or `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient` without an explicit endpoint).
162. 
163. > **Important — the factory must opt into user-secrets explicitly.** In a
164. > `dotnet test` process the entry assembly is `testhost.exe`, so the
165. > `dotnet user-secrets` payload tied to *your* `UserSecretsId` is NOT auto
166. > loaded by `Host.CreateApplicationBuilder()`. The Case A template above
167. > calls `builder.Configuration.AddUserSecrets(typeof(...).Assembly)` for
168. > this reason. Without that line, the secret is set on disk but never read.
169. 
170. Recommend the user wire one of:
171. 
172. ```pwsh
173. # 0 — one-time: bind the test project to a secrets store
174. dotnet user-secrets init --project <App>.Evals.Tests
175.

 works without further code. Detection result is surfaced in step 2

 ## Patterns to scan for
 
 Scan **`*.AppHost.csproj` directory** and **all `*.Agent*.csproj`
 directories**. Match (case-insensitive, multi-line):
 
 | Pattern (regex-ish) | Inferred client | Example file:line |
 |---------------------|-----------------|--------------------|
 | `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient\s*\(` or `AddAzureOpenAIClient\s*\(` | Azure OpenAI | `AppHost.cs`, `Program.cs` |
 | `AddOpenAIChatClient\s*\(` | OpenAI direct | `Program.cs` |
 | `AddOllamaChatClient\s*\(` | Ollama | `Program.cs` |
 | `AddAIInference\s*\(` (Foundry deployment alias) | Azure AI Foundry | `AppHost.cs` |
 | `AddAzureChatCompletionsClient\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\.AddChatClient\s*\(` | Aspire `Aspire.Azure.AI.Inference` (Foundry-routed, **legacy — see deprecation note below**) | `Program.cs` |
 | `AddOpenAIClient\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\.AddChatClient\s*\(` | Aspire OpenAI/v1 (Foundry-routed via the OpenAI SDK) | `Program.cs` |
 | `services\.AddSingleton<IChatClient>` (any explicit registration) | custom | varies |
 | `\.AsIChatClient\(\)` (after an SDK client) | manual wrap | varies |
 
 > The `AddAzureChatCompletionsClient(...).AddChatClient(...)` chain is the
 > Aspire 13.2 way of wiring an `IChatClient` against a Foundry chat
 > deployment via the `Azure.AI.Inference` beta SDK. The argument is the
 > **connection-string name**, which Aspire's AppHost populates
 > automatically (`AddDeployment("chat", ...)` -> connection string `chat`).
 > The factory mirrors both calls verbatim.
 >
 > ⚠️ **Deprecation note (as of 2026):** the `Azure.AI.Inference` beta SDK
 > is being retired on **August 26, 2026** in favor of the GA OpenAI/v1
 > API + stable OpenAI SDK. New apps should prefer the
 > `AddOpenAIClient(...).AddChatClient(...)` pattern against an OpenAI/v1
 > endpoint, which avoids several quirks (notably the reasoning-model
 > `max_tokens` rejection documented in
 > `references/common-pitfalls.md`). The skill still detects and supports
 > the legacy pattern unchanged. See the
 > [Foundry migration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/model-inference-to-openai-migration).

 ```csharp
 {

     /// Resolves the same IChatClient the app uses, by building a minimal
     /// host that mirrors the app's DI registration.
     /// Detected: {{DetectionSummary}} at {{File}}:{{Line}}

     public static IChatClient Create()

         // user-secrets are NOT auto-loaded by CreateApplicationBuilder.
         // Add them explicitly from THIS assembly's UserSecretsId.
 ```

 `ReportingConfig` picks agent client based on tier:
